text:
zoe: :rotating_light: getting pinged by CardioPay support — they're seeing a sustained stream of 429s since ~11:23 UTC in ap-southeast-1. Affected customers report failed checkout callbacks.
alerts-bot: Alert: rate_limit_exceeded for api_key=cp_live_XXX region=ap-southeast-1 429_count=2,134 window=10m
devon: copying logs now — initial look shows a high burst of identical POST /v1/generate requests from a handful of IPs, all using the same api_key. Is CardioPay using a single shared key for all merchant subaccounts?
zoe: AFAIK yes — their integration uses one API key per merchant org and fans out on-prem. CSM says spike correlates with a marketing email at 11:20.
kevin: quick check: our gateway token-bucket for that key is max_rpm=1200 and tpm cap=30000. With the fanout they hit the bucket quickly -> token shortfall -> 429s. Logs show limiter reason=burst and limiter_type=per_key_token_bucket.
amy: customer sent sample response headers — we return `Retry-After: 30` currently. They have an aggressive retry loop (no jitter) so it's amplifying. Here's their provided snippet:

```
retries = 0
while retries < 5:
    resp = post('/v1/generate')
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        sleep(1)  # <-- too tight, immediate retry
        retries += 1
    else:
        break
```

sylvia: yeah that's classic retry storm. Immediate mitigation options: 1) ask CardioPay to add exponential backoff + jitter, 2) create a temporary route override to raise RPM for that key, 3) apply ingress shaping at their proxy to smooth bursts. Which do we want to do now?
devon: ops action: can we lift per-key RPM to 3000 for the next 30 minutes while they throttle? Command I ran to inspect metrics: 

```
rctl metrics get --key cp_live_XXX --window 5m --metric requests_per_minute
```

current: 2100rpm sustained. If we bump to 3000 we'll stop immediate 429s but won't fix client retry pattern.
kevin: I can apply a short-lived override. Doing `gatewayctl override set --key cp_live_XXX --rpm 3000 --duration 30m --reason "support: marketing blast mitigation"`

Note: also enabling per-route smoothing (leaky-bucket per upstream IP) so their fanout doesn't collapse our buckets.
amy: applied the override, metrics show 429s dropping within 40s. :thumbsup: I've also added a temporary alert: CardioPay_high_429s -> page if 429_rate > 100/min for 5m.
zoe: CSM will reach out to CardioPay and request immediate client fix (exp backoff + jitter + respect Retry-After). Can we prepare a short suggested code snippet for them?
sylvia: yes — suggest this patch:

```
# exponential backoff with jitter
import random, time
for attempt in range(6):
    resp = post('/v1/generate')
    if resp.status_code != 429:
        break
    backoff = min(60, (2 ** attempt))
    jitter = random.uniform(0, backoff * 0.1)
    time.sleep(backoff + jitter)
```

Also recommend checking they rotate to per-subaccount API keys rather than one monolithic key.
devon: logging follow-up: saved audit logs + request traces to /internal/archives/cardio_1839001111.log and flagged for postmortem.
kevin: added a routing rule to throttle individual source IPs to 200rpm to prevent single hosts from draining the token bucket. Also added a fallback model route (smaller model) to keep latency-sensitive flows functional under heavy load.
amy: Customer CSM update: CardioPay acknowledged their retry bug and will deploy fix in next 2 hours. I've scheduled a canary check and will remove override once 429s stable < 5/min for 15m.
zoe: closing loop — please add this to the incident tracker and assign postmortem to devon+amy. Make sure to include request traces + suggested code snippet. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
